lessons: In crypto, sell straddles far outside the recent range: premium is fat and breakevens can span the whole historical range.
Rolling 20% monthly returns on ~$4,000 margin shows how high IV compensates sellers — size such trades small.

title_clean: Claim Your Refund! NSE Slams Brokers for Margin Penalty Scam
summary: Explains NSE circular ref 602022 (2 Sep 2022) reiterating that brokers cannot pass peak margin penalty (short-collection of upfront margin) to clients, and must refund any such penalty charged after 11 Oct 2021. Recaps his earlier RTI to SEBI proving no client-level peak margin penalty exists. Alleges (unconfirmed) that brokers inflate mandated margins ~3% to avoid triggering penalties, and urges traders to audit ledgers and demand refunds.
lessons: Read your broker ledger: peak margin penalties levied on clients are illegal — circular-cited refunds are claimable.
If a broker partially refunds a penalty, it proves the deduction was never legitimate — it should be zero.

event_claims.claim: NSE circular 602022 dated 2 Sep 2022: members not permitted to pass on clearing-corporation penalties for short/non-collection of upfront margin to clients; refunds mandated for penalties passed on after 11 Oct 2021; references earlier circulars of 31 Jul 2020 and 12 Oct (2021)
SEBI clarified via RTI response that peak margin penalty must be paid by broker, not client
One top Indian broker allegedly raised charged margins ~3% above exchange-mandated levels to avoid peak-margin breach (speaker states unconfirmed)

summary: Compact contrast of option buyer vs seller: buyer pays small premium in cash with low win probability; seller posts large margin but can fund it with collateral; buyer can be right on direction yet lose to premium decay, while seller can be wrong on view yet still profit if price stays inside breakevens.
lessons: The seller's edge is statistical cushion: being wrong on direction but right on range still pays.
Buyers risk capital in cash; sellers can post collateral — a capital-efficiency asymmetry few beginners grasp.

title_clean: Reason for Gap Up and Gap Down
summary: Explains that pre-open price discovery (call auction roughly 9:00–9:08) rather than overnight news alone produces the opening print: orders can be placed but not matched during pre-open; matching occurs at 9:15, creating gaps.
lessons: Gaps are manufactured in the pre-open auction: overnight sentiment expresses as imbalance that resolves at 9:15.

title_clean: Sometimes Value Stocks Are Better Than Growth Stocks
summary: Contrasts growth vs value stocks (expansion reinvestment vs high dividend payout). Traces his own value-picking record: 2014 TV-era picks (Balmer Lawrie, Rane group, Tata Investment Corp), and recent calls — ITC (~₹200→₹300+), REC (~₹110, 1:3 bonus, ~10% yield), PFC (~10% yield), Tata Investment Corp (~₹1,500–1,600→₹2,700 in ~10 days). Presents the conservative HNI combo: value stock + ~10% dividend + covered call ≈ 30% p.a. with dividend-yield-based downside cushion; notes lot-size capital gates (~₹8 lakh for REC).
lessons: A 10–11% dividend yield creates its own floor: at half the price the yield doubles to 20–25%, drawing buyers before catastrophe.
Conservative compounding: value stock (~10% capital + ~10% dividend) plus covered-call income approaches ~30% p.a. at low risk.
Cyclical high-yielders (Vedanta, Tata Steel) are not value stocks — the yield compensates for wide price cycles.

title_clean: If You Don't Close Future Positions
summary: Short rule video: letting futures expire unmanaged is fine for index futures (cash-settled) but stock futures result in physical delivery obligations; always square up yourself.
lessons: Index futures cash-settle harmlessly; stock futures expire into delivery — never let a stock future ride to expiry unmanaged.
